question.text: Which bond provides the PERFECT immunization against interest rate risk for a 10-year liability, theoretically?

explanation.text: The Logic: A zero-coupon bond has no interim cash flows, so its Macaulay duration equals its maturity. A 10-year zero-coupon bond therefore locks the future value of the 10-year liability without interest-rate risk or reinvestment risk, which the workbook identifies as theoretically the best immunizing portfolio. The Trap: A 10-year coupon-paying bond has duration shorter than its maturity because of coupon cash flows, and a 20-year bond with duration around 10 still has reinvestment risk on coupons. A floating-rate bond resets to market and does not lock the future value of a 10-year liability. Note: Pages 340-342 establish duration matching for immunization and identify a maturity-matched zero-coupon bond as the theoretical ideal.
